title: Java Instrumentation retransformClasses
description: The java.lang.instrument API lets a Java agent rewrite already-loaded classes while the JVM runs. An agent registered at startup (or attached later) calls Instrumentation.retransformClasses with new bytecode, and existing instances keep running with patched method bodies — the standard way production JVMs hot-fix code without downtime.
method: A -javaagent premain registers a ClassFileTransformer; later, retransformClasses triggers re-transformation of target classes and the JVM swaps method bodies atomically at a safepoint, preserving object identity.

specification.constraint: schema changes (new fields) need full redefinition support

usage: Attach the agent, point it at the class list, and ship patched bytecode over JMX or a control socket; verify with a canary instance before fleet-wide rollout.

demo.code:
import subprocess
code='''public class Hot { public static String v(){ return "v1"; } }'''
open('/tmp/Hot.java','w').write(code)
subprocess.run(['javac','/tmp/Hot.java'], check=False)
print('Compiled Hot.java — retransformClasses() would now swap v() body at runtime via a javaagent.')

title: Erlang code server hot upgrade
description: Erlang/OTP was built for telecom switches that never stop: the code server keeps two versions of every module (current and old), and a release handler swaps them while processes keep running. Fully-qualified calls (mod:fun()) resolve to the newest version, so upgrades apply to new calls immediately.
method: code:purge/1 and code:load_file/1 manage current/old module versions; gen_server code_change callbacks migrate process state between versions during a release upgrade.
usage: Build a release with systools, write appup instructions with code_change handlers, and apply with release_handler:install_release.

demo.code:
print('Erlang hot upgrade sequence:')
seq = [('code:load_file(mymod)', 'load new beam'), ('release_handler:install_release', 'swap versions'), ('gen_server code_change', 'migrate state')]
for cmd, what in seq:
    print(f'  {cmd}  -> {what}')
print('Old code kept until last old-version process finishes.')

title: eBPF uprobe live patching
description: eBPF programs attached as uprobes run inside the kernel when a userspace function executes, letting operators observe — and with bpf_override_return, alter — behavior of running binaries without touching the binary or restarting it. Used for live fault injection and behavior overrides in production.
method: bpf() loads a verified eBPF program and attaches it to a userspace symbol; the program runs in kernel context at function entry and can override the return value for whitelisted functions.
usage: Compile the probe with clang -target bpf, attach to the target symbol, and gate overrides behind a feature flag checked in the probe.

title: ByteBuddy runtime subclassing
description: ByteBuddy is a Java bytecode generation library that creates classes, subclasses, and redefinitions at runtime without writing .class files by hand. Frameworks use it for proxies, mocks (Mockito), and agents that need programmatic bytecode with a type-safe DSL.
method: ByteBuddy().redefine(Class).method(named("x")).intercept(FixedValue.value(...)).make().load(...) builds new bytecode in memory and loads it through the instrumentation API or a child classloader.
usage: Define matchers for the target methods, pick an interception (FixedValue, MethodDelegation, Advice), and install with an AgentBuilder for retransformation.

demo.code:
print('ByteBuddy redefinition recipe:')
recipe = [
    'new ByteBuddy()',
    '.redefine(OrderService.class)',
    '.method(named("total"))',
    '.intercept(FixedValue.value(0))  // patched behavior',
]
print('\n'.join('  ' + r for r in recipe))
print('Result: total() now returns 0 in the running JVM.')

title: Custom ClassLoader defineClass swap
description: Java application servers (Tomcat, OSGi containers) achieve hot deployment with throwaway child classloaders: new code loads in a fresh loader, traffic shifts over, and the old loader is garbage collected. The JVM never redefines anything — isolation does the work.
method: URLClassLoader subclass overrides loadClass for hot packages; redeploy creates a new loader instance reading updated jars, then swaps the reference; stale classes die with the old loader once unreferenced.
usage: Version each deployment unit, load in an isolated loader, drain in-flight requests, then drop the old loader reference.

demo.code:
import importlib.util
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_loader('hotunit_v2', loader=None)
print('Child-loader strategy: fresh loader per version.')
print('spec name:', spec.name, '-> traffic shifts here; old loader GC\'d when drained.')

title: WebAssembly module live swap
description: WebAssembly instances are cheap to create and link, so hosts hot-swap modules by instantiating the new .wasm and re-pointing imported function tables. Runtimes like Wasmtime support swapping without dropping the host process, giving native-speed hot reload for sandboxed plugins.
method: Compile new wasm bytes to a Module, instantiate with the same import object, then atomically replace the instance reference; in-flight calls finish on the old instance.
usage: Version wasm artifacts, keep the import ABI stable, and swap instances behind a mutex or RCU pointer.

demo.code:
print('WASM live swap:')
steps = ['wat2wasm plugin_v2.wat -o plugin_v2.wasm', 'instantiate with same imports', 'atomic pointer swap', 'old instance dropped']
for s in steps:
    print('  ' + s)
print('Host process never restarted.')

title: Frida dynamic instrumentation
description: Frida injects a JavaScript engine into running processes and lets analysts hook functions, replace implementations, and rewrite arguments on the fly. It is the standard dynamic-analysis tool for mobile and desktop binaries: no source, no restart, live interception.
method: frida.attach(pid) injects frida-agent; Interceptor.attach hooks native functions and Java.perform hooks JVM/ART methods, running user JS inside the target to read/write memory and call originals.
usage: Write a hook script, attach to the target PID, and stream intercepted calls back over Frida's message channel for analysis.

title: .NET Edit and Continue
description: The .NET runtime supports Edit-and-Continue: while debugging, the compiler emits a metadata delta and the CLR applies it to the running process. MetadataUpdateHandler and System.Reflection.Metadata allow libraries to react to applied updates, and hot reload extends this to running apps without a debugger.
method: Roslyn produces an ENC delta (added/changed IL + metadata); the CLR's ApplyUpdate walks the delta, patches method bodies, and invokes [ModuleInitializer]-style update handlers so static state can refresh.
usage: Use dotnet watch for dev loops; for production, expose a controlled update endpoint that validates the delta signature before applying.
